steps.content: 000's expression stiffens, and she staggers as if injured. This definitely wasn't caused by you.
She quickly covers it up. This reaction piques your interest. It's the first time you've seen her hide something.
...Forget it, I'm not in the mood anymore. Let's call it quits.
With a wave of her hand, the Assassin Zone dissipates, and 000 vanishes.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Request received. The target is nearby. Initiating teleportation.

steps.speaker: Labyrinth
steps.content: Chief!

steps.speaker: Cat
steps.content: Meow!

Your companion's shout doesn't catch up with you. The next second, as your consciousness returns, you find yourself in another space. The invisible glass wall that had been suppressing your body disappears.
It's a deeper data space, with bizarre characters floating around. You don't understand their meaning, but you feel an inexplicable aversion.
Amid the data and files, 000 sits at the end with her back to you. She senses your arrival but doesn’t turn around; instead, she slightly covers the wound on her arm. She appears unusually quiet.
Sigh... why are you still following me?
I'm not in a good mood right now. I'll hang out with you some time later.
...Still here? When I'm in a bad mood, I tend to throw a tantrum. It's better that you stay away.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: I'm here to see what's bothering you.
It's rare to see you so vulnerable.

steps.content: She smiles, hooks her pinky around yours, then clasps your palm. She takes your hand and shuffles to your side.
Hehe, what a kind and gentle Chief.
You really think I won't do anything to you?
Oh... if you want to attack me, you'll have to get closer.
As soon as she finishes speaking, she flips you to the ground. Data from the void gathers into bundles, binding your wrists, waist, and ankles.
000 supports herself on your shoulder and looks down at you. Her knee presses against your chest, and before you can speak, she raises her hand to cover your mouth.
You let your guard down too easily around Sinners. Is it because you met too many good people in the past? Or was my acting too superb?

Those cute ducks were just there to confuse you. The games along the way were just for my amusement. Even this little girl persona is something I took from the DisCity dark web. You know what kind of place that is, don't you?
A strange sensation spreads as data turbulence corrodes your body, making you feel nauseous. The force in her hand gradually increases, and you see a familiar madness in her eyes.
I'm not your average person. I'm perfectly comfortable with appreciating your uniqueness while harboring a desire to kill you.
If I can kill the gods and replace them, what is stopping me from doing the same to you?
You struggle a bit and release your shackles, but it doesn't help at all.
She stares at you for a while. Just when you start to feel suffocated, she suddenly lets go.
Okay, I was just kidding.
She releases her hand.
Sinners don't have to be that bad.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: I know what this place is.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This place holds a vast amount of records, detailing everyone's origins, experiences, abilities, preferences, relationships, and even their values and potential future developments. It's more detailed than the Bureau's records.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But you must be thinking, "Not only that. The gods dictate everything."
Haha, yes, the gods dictate everything, including your past, present, and future. Whether it's pain or happiness, they dictate how you experience the world.
Every decision you think you made of your own volition, every path you walked, was actually written by them without exception... but you surely don't believe that.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'd rather believe they installed cameras to spy on our every move and then secretly recorded it all in these documents.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If you claim our original world is a massive game that I shouldn't believe in, then the stories you're telling me could be lies meant to deceive me.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: After all, everyone should choose their own truth by listening to their heart.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Besides, if everything is their creation...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Then why would they create someone like me, who doesn’t believe in them, and someone like you, whom they can’t control? If everyone is their marionette, how do you explain your desire to kill them?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Would they create someone who would want to overturn them?
You have a point.
She looks up at you.
Do you want to see the fate they had in store for me? The "file" they wrote for me?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...I'm not falling for it. If I say yes, you'll try to get me to kill one of them with you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Just tell me. If you believe in fate as determined by the gods, you surely haven't forgotten what they’ve written for you.
A smile shows on her face.
Yes, I remember everything they designed for 000. It's all too simple.
Family: Blank. Education: Blank. Likes, dislikes, fears: Blank. Related characters and events: Blank.
Beliefs? None. Ideals? None. Even the gods don't know what I've experienced since my creation.
If you don't believe me, we can kill this god, take the permissions, and see that version of "me."
Oh... but don't go to where the Sinners are. I wasn't put there.
Go to "Early Settings," look for a file called "[Discarded]CharacterSettings_000.xlsx," and there you'll find everything the gods had for me.
It's something unfinished, something forgotten.
After me, the gods created one Sinner after another, giving them souls and lives, but they never looked at me again.
Well? Is this experience good enough for you?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Do you hate them for abandoning you?
Vengeance? Hahaha, how could I? They never even told me what hate is. How could I seek vengeance?
${PlayerName}, I'm glad you're willing to get to know me, and conversing with me as if I were a human being. But ultimately, I'm something else.
As a Sinner, I wasn't given any beliefs, emotions, or motivations.
So when Mania spread into this space, it took over the empty me effortlessly.
The genius who invented the DisCity dark web could digitalize everything and merge all data into the Mania network, while Mania itself... could cross boundaries and reach rifts in other worlds.
The corrupted data thus reached the abandoned file, filling up all its emptiness, and then created a Sinner that was never meant to exist.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I get it now... You've been overtaken by Mania, which is why you caused all this mayhem. You're driven by the mastermind of the dark web, spurred by Mania, right?
Hahah, now it's your turn to deny my own free will? "Everything might be fake, but we can choose what's real with our hearts." Haha.
She wipes away her tears of laughter.
Since I became conscious, I realized I'm different from other Sinners. They can go to the big world, but I'm trapped in a small grid.
When I finally became a Sinner through Mania, I was immediately deemed a system error by the gods. They constantly tried to hunt me down and erase me, forcing me to hide in the rifts of the dark web.

After learning the underlying logic of the world from the sea of dark web data, learning to edit code to avoid detection, and launching rewinds to save myself, I finally stepped out of the dark web and got to see the world I've longed for as I pleased...

But I couldn't see the beauty anymore. I saw layers upon layers of code behind everything. The world I once yearned for is nothing more than a game created from a higher dimension. The sky has a limit, and there's only one path into the future. The gods have already dictated all possibilities.
...But fortunately, soon after that, I met you.
I don't know why, but from you, I can see the destiny set by the gods and feel the connection from them.

"This person can take me to a bigger world"... Hehe, every time the gods close all the doors on me, I always manage to find a tiny crack. You made this possible for me. The moment I saw you, I made my decision.
So, ${PlayerName}, knowing all this, what do you think I'm up to next?

steps.speaker: Choice
options: ...It isn't our world that you want.

steps.content: If our world is but a game in your eyes, then ruling it means nothing to you...
You brought me to this new world because, for you, only this new world can be considered real.
You want to establish yourself here. And I, along with my world, are just tools for you. You used me to reach here, and my world...
You want to take over my world because there's something valuable in it. What you want is...
At this very moment, the data space suddenly shatters, plunging you into darkness, but it also frees you from her control.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: A field trip to the Otherworld, chaperoned by a great teacher... What a spectacular opportunity!

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: You're of age now. It's time to step out of your little shadow, broaden your horizons, and see the bigger world!

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Okay okay, I got it. That Chief seems to be in trouble. If you can't find any ink, then just give way to my little shadows.
The shadows on the wall travel through various surfaces, bringing about large patches of darkness and... cheers. Bystanders excitedly watch on, thinking it's some special light show.
(Scene change)
Looking at the lively scene outside, 000 lets out a sigh.
...Causing such a ruckus again. They're really something, charging around recklessly, and not letting me relax for a moment.
Chief, get ready, I'm going to rewind.
Sometimes you just can't help it, but we still keep going nevertheless.
We're alike. We both understand this very well.
